text: Lir (Lear) is an Irish hero and the father in the story of the Children of Lir. The great Irish sea god Manannán was called mac Lir, which means son of Lir. Yet it is not entirely clear who Lir himself was. Some scholars think he was a former sea deity taken into the myths of an invading people. Lir is read for his children, changed by their stepmother Aífe into swans, and for the Three Sorrows of Ireland.

okr.objective: Give a clear account of Lir and his family place in Celtic myth.
